page: Microsoft Azure F48als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB RAM, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache structure includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The system features AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions. It does not include dedicated GPUs or bundled local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute scaling across multi-threaded operations. In stress-ng, the server reaches a top-tier multi-core score of 147,786.21 alongside a strong single-core result of 3,080.29. Geekbench tests follow this trend with a multi-core score of 24,068.0, led by high-throughput results in software compilation with Clang (64,381.0) and image processing (18,661.0). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 629.27 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% of tested profiles. Memory throughput is also consistent, providing 226.93 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 144.12 GB/sec in write operations.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the F48als_v6 cost-effective for pure parallel compute workloads that do not require extensive memory capacity. Because it avoids the expense of unused RAM allocations, the instance maximizes efficiency per compute cycle for CPU-bound tasks. However, workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets or low-latency local NVMe scratch space will need attached remote premium storage, representing a functional tradeoff.

This server profile fits compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, code compilation, video or image processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-concurrency static web serving. It also functions well for distributed batch processing and CPU-focused scientific simulations.
description: Microsoft Azure F48als_v6 is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 48 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 cores at 3.7 GHz and 96.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio on an x86_64 architecture. The server has no local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing shows top-tier multi-core throughput, recording 147,786.21 in stress-ng multi-core and 24,068.0 in Geekbench multi-core, with outstanding Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression rates. Memory bandwidth achieves 226.93 GB/sec on uncached large reads. With vector acceleration including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, the F48als_v6 provides high computational density without the overhead of excess memory allocation. It is well-matched for parallel compute jobs, large-scale software compilation, batch processing, image manipulation, and CPU-based inference workloads.
